passage: Friday evening, the accounts office was half empty when Tanvir stopped at Sudha's desk. "You're my best analyst. Nobody else can fix this month-end file. The whole team will suffer if you're not in tomorrow." Sudha's stomach dropped. Tomorrow was her cousin's engagement lunch. She felt guilty already, and a little flattered too. She had heard the same praise three weekends in a row, and her review still said nothing about extra work. "Sir, will this be counted in my review? And can I take Monday morning off?" Tanvir waved his hand. "We'll see, we'll see." Sudha picked up her bag. "I can do two hours tomorrow morning, not the whole day. After that I have a family event." He frowned, but nodded. 😔

qa.a: It was Sudha's cousin's engagement lunch.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Sudha have when Tanvir praised her?
qa.a: She felt guilty and a little flattered at the same time, and her stomach dropped.

qa.q: What did Sudha do to test whether the praise was real?
qa.a: She asked whether the extra work would count in her review and whether she could take Monday morning off, then offered a clear limit of two hours.

qa.q: How might Tanvir see Sudha's answer?
qa.a: He may feel annoyed, since he frowned, but he still agreed, which suggests her limit was clear enough to accept.

grounding: A boss uses praise and guilt to get extra work; the worker checks the reward and negotiates a clear limit.
